Logo

The Lockup

The primary identity is the BMC | COLLECTIVE lockup — the Darren Hardy / Business Master Class seal, a divider, and the COLLECTIVE wordmark. Use the supplied artwork only; never rebuild it.

White — on dark / photographic backgrounds
Black — on light backgrounds

Clear space & minimum size

Keep clear space around the lockup equal to at least half the height of the seal on all sides. Minimum width: 160 px on screen so the seal text stays legible. On the site it renders crisp at large scale (artwork is 2030 px wide).

Do

  • White on dark or photographic backgrounds.
  • Black on light backgrounds.
  • Preserve proportions and clear space.

Don't

  • Recolor, add gradients, shadows, or outlines.
  • Stretch, condense, rotate, or crop the seal.
  • Place white on light or black on dark.
  • Rebuild or rearrange the seal and wordmark.

Color

Color System

A near-monochrome, dark foundation with one chromatic accent applied sparingly. Premium comes from restraint, not decoration.

Cyan on dark
Accent, emphasis, em.key, titles, play buttons & ghost CTAs live on dark surfaces.
Plum on light
The same accent idea, re-hued so it reads premium on light. Emphasis & titles on bone/white.

The one rule that governs the page: Cyan reads loud and washed-out on light; plum reads premium there (and would vanish on dark). Same idea, two hues.

Accessibility

White & Silver on Black/Ink pass AA. Ink/Muted on Bone/White pass AA. Cyan is for accent on dark, not body text; plum for accent on light. Verify new pairings at 4.5:1.

Typography

Inter — everything. One typeface, no exceptions. Hierarchy is built from weight, size, case, letter-spacing, and color — never a second family. Display, eyebrows, labels, and titles are UPPERCASE; body and quotes are sentence case.

Ambient wash (background only)

Low-opacity purple/magenta radial gradients behind a dark section to add depth. Background only — never on type, icons, or borders.

Elevation

Motion

Scroll-reveal (fade-up ~28–40px) + count-up stats. Premium easing cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). No bounce/spin. Honors prefers-reduced-motion.

Web

Web Implementation

The live tokens. Reference variables — never hard-code raw hex in components.

/* Design tokens — from the live :root */
:root{
  /* neutrals */
  --black:#0a0a0a; --ink:#141414; --surface-card:#0e0c12;
  --white:#ffffff; --bone:#f5f5f5; --silver:#b8b8b8; --muted:#444;
  /* brand — rgba(var(--x-rgb), a) for any opacity */
  --bmc-cyan-rgb:120,228,239;   --bmc-plum-rgb:75,44,106;
  --bmc-purple-rgb:156,39,172; --bmc-magenta-rgb:214,42,143;
  --gold:#f5b301; /* review stars only */
  --radius:4px; --section-pad-mobile:72px;
}

Layout & spacing

Container max 1380 px; side padding 48 px desktop / 24 px mobile.

Sections breathe: 120–200 px vertical on desktop (climax largest); uniform 72 px on mobile.

Tighten and unify spacing on mobile; let desktop breathe.

Accent logic (load-bearing)

Cyan on dark · Plum on light. Functional cyan UI stays cyan on media.

Accessibility

Body ≥ 4.5:1. Visible focus, alt text, prefers-reduced-motion honored.

Performance

Self-host Inter (no third-party calls), inline critical CSS, WebP imagery, lazy below-fold media, defer video players to first scroll — keeps mobile PageSpeed in the 90s.

Type

Emphasis & Word Craft

How brand phrases earn weight without italics. A single mechanic — color-shift, never font-style — applies at both headline and body-text tiers.

Rule 1 · Never italics

The brand never uses italics. The <em> element is used semantically to mark emphasized phrases, but its default italic is overridden. Emphasis comes from a color shift only.

Rule 2 · Em color-shift

Emphasized phrases render in the brand red --accent: #B72A30. The accent was tuned up from the original #A0252B after testing: at the original luminance, red against black had only ~3:1 contrast versus white-on-black's ~21:1, which created an optical illusion where the red text read visually thinner than the surrounding white. The brighter #B72A30 closes that gap on dark backgrounds while staying brand-correct on bone.

/* Em color-shift — applies to every emphasized phrase, headlines + body alike */
.subhero-title em, .collage-title em, .team-title em,
.values-title em, .beliefs-title em, .beliefs-foot em,
.recruit-video-title em, .process-title em,
.closing-headline em, .creed-quote em, .positions-header em {
  font-style: normal;          /* override the browser italic */
  color: var(--accent);     /* #B72A30 */
  text-shadow:                       /* Rule 3 — see below */
    0.4px 0 0 currentColor,
    -0.4px 0 0 currentColor,
    0 0.4px 0 currentColor,
    0 -0.4px 0 currentColor,
    0 0 0.6px currentColor;
}

Rule 3 · Contrast-weight compensation

Even at the brighter accent, red text has lower luminance contrast against backgrounds than white or black does. The eye reads lower-contrast type as visually thinner at the same font-weight. The five-shadow stack synthesizes ~0.4 px of ink on every glyph edge plus a 0.6 px soft blur — roughly a full font-weight worth of apparent stroke thickness — so the red phrase reads at the same visual heft as its surrounding type. The shadows use currentColor so the rule works identically wherever it's applied.

Rule 4 · Punctuation placement

Closing punctuation goes outside the em: <em>Stand Beside</em>.  not  <em>Stand Beside.</em>. Exception: when the punctuation is part of a quoted exclamation, it lives inside the em (e.g. "<em>Hell Yeah!</em>").

Rule 5 · Distribute emphasis around connectors

When two emphasized phrases share a connector ("&", "and", "but"), each phrase gets its own em — the connector stays neutral. Example: Our <em>Core Values</em> & <em>Attributes</em>. The "&" reads as scaffolding, not a brand word.

Brand term protection · .nobreak

Multi-word brand terms (primary example: A-Team) must never break across lines. A single utility class enforces this:

/* Typography utility — phrases that must never break across lines */
.nobreak { white-space: nowrap; }

Wrap usage:

Join The <em class="nobreak">A-Team</em>.
Meet The <span class="nobreak">A-Team</span>
Want To Join<br>The <span class="nobreak">A-Team</span>?

Wrap A-Team in every visible rendered context: HTML body text, JS-injected templates, dynamic component output. Do not wrap inside meta tags, alt attributes, page titles, HTML/JS comments, or JSON-LD — those don't render visually. Reuse the same class for any other brand phrase that must hold together (e.g. BMC|COLLECTIVE in flowing text).

UI

CTA System

Two button variants share identical dimensions and motion — only the paint differs. Use them deliberately based on what the page moment needs to ask of the visitor.

.btn-solid · Demands action

Filled — white background, black text, white border. On hover the fill drops out and the type flips. Use as the page's primary or closing CTA where you want maximum visual weight (closing-page conversions, the final commit-point on a posting page).

.btn-ghost · Invites without pressuring

Outlined — transparent background, white text, white border. On hover the background fills white and the type flips to black. Use in headers and secondary slots where you want presence without demanding immediate action (subhero CTAs, ambient navigation moments).

/* Shared dimensions, font, padding, transition */
.btn-solid, .btn-ghost {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px;
  padding: 20px 40px;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px;
  letter-spacing: 0.24em; text-transform: uppercase;
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: all 0.2s;
  border: 1px solid var(--white);
}
/* Only the paint differs */
.btn-solid { background: var(--white); color: var(--black); }
.btn-solid:hover { background: transparent; color: var(--white); }
.btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--white); }
.btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--white); color: var(--black); }
/* Arrow nudges on hover for both variants */
.btn-solid .arrow, .btn-ghost .arrow { transition: transform 0.2s; }
.btn-solid:hover .arrow, .btn-ghost:hover .arrow { transform: translateX(3px); }

A page can host both: a ghost CTA in the header (low-pressure invite) and a solid CTA in the closing section (the actual conversion). On bone-background sections, invert the swatch references (solid becomes black-on-bone, ghost gets the dark outline) so the contrast logic stays the same.

IA

Recruiting & Careers

Patterns that emerged building the A-Team careers experience. Codified for re-use as the family of recruiting pages grows.

Per-page rightmost nav slot

The last slot in the top nav is context-dependent — it always points the visitor to the most useful next step for their current location. This is the only nav item that changes per page.

Home                           → "Start Here"          → #start-here
Careers                        → "Open Positions"      → #open-positions (same-page anchor)
<role> posting pages           → "Open Positions"      → careers.html#open-positions
All other subpages             → "Start Here"          → home.html#start-here

Pattern: the rightmost slot always answers "what should this visitor do next from where they are?" — the home page converts toward Darren's free resources; pages inside the careers funnel convert toward the actual open seats.

URL structure

Job posting pages nest under /careers/ rather than living as flat siblings. URL hierarchy mirrors content hierarchy, which simplifies the nav rule above to a single-prefix check and lets sitemaps / breadcrumbs / analytics fall out of the URL itself.

/                              home
/about
/careers                       careers landing
  /careers/content-marketer
  /careers/marketing-campaign-manager
  /careers/member-experience-specialist
/resources

Team grid · dynamic filler CTA

The team grid uses a CSS grid at 4 cols / 3 cols / 2 cols at desktop / tablet / mobile. Because team count won't always divide evenly into the breakpoint columns, a single CTA card (.team-cta) is appended after the last person card and its grid-column: span N is computed in JS to fill the remaining cells of the last row. When the grid divides evenly, the CTA takes a full row of its own at the bottom — it's always present.

// Run on load and on resize (debounced)
function getCols() {
  if (window.matchMedia('(max-width: 720px)').matches) return 2;
  if (window.matchMedia('(max-width: 1080px)').matches) return 3;
  return 4;
}
function fitCta() {
  const cols = getCols();
  const rem = team.length % cols;
  cta.style.gridColumn = `span ${rem === 0 ? cols : (cols - rem)}`;
}

The CTA card itself drops aspect-ratio and relies on grid's default align-self: stretch so its bottom edge aligns with the person cards in the same row (photo + name/role meta height). A min-height: 240px fallback applies when the CTA is alone in a full-width row. Use grid-template-columns: repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr)) — without the explicit 0 minimum, cell content can force overflow on mobile.

Member-services CTA visual

Card background sits in mid-grey (--grey #888888), not red — blends with the greyscale team photo backgrounds. Red appears only as a small 2 px accent bar above the headline (matching the values cards' marker). White headline, ghost button. Hover darkens to --grey-soft, the accent bar grows 28 px → 48 px, the button inverts to white-fill + black-text. Red is the spice, not the meal.
